title: Layered SLO contract with predictive burn gating and graceful degradation playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Define a multi-layer SLA/SLO contract for hosted inference that combines latency envelopes, availability targets, and an error-budget-driven rollout gate system with predictive burn-rate detection and a documented graceful degradation playbook.
background: Existing SLO tickets cover static thresholds and basic canary gates. We need a single contract that (1) maps SLOs to product tiers, (2) prescribes automated canary gating behavior tied to predictive burn detection, and (3) defines allowed degradation actions and rollback criteria. This is intended to reduce manual SRE intervention during rollouts and to standardize customer communications.
scope_included: Define SLO numbers for interactive chat, stream-first-token, and embeddings for Standard/Premium/Dedicated tiers
Specify availability targets and monthly error budgets per tier
Design rollout gates leveraging predictive burn-rate (short-window rapid-detection) and sustained burn thresholds
Document graceful degradation actions (model fallback, quantized variant route, reduced max_tokens) and order of operations
Acceptance criteria and required dashboards/alerts for Console and PagerDuty runbook
scope_excluded: Changes to runtime kernel implementations (ENG tickets will follow)
Billing changes for overages (handled by Finance)
slo_definitions: Hosted Standard - Chat interactive: P95 first-token latency <= 300ms, P50 per-token latency <= 40ms
Hosted Premium - Chat interactive: P95 first-token latency <= 180ms, P50 per-token latency <= 30ms
Hosted Dedicated - Chat interactive: P95 first-token latency <= 120ms (contractable), P50 per-token latency <= 20ms
Embeddings: P95 request latency <= 200ms for Standard, <=120ms Premium
Error budget: Standard 0.05% monthly, Premium 0.01% monthly (translate to minutes per month)
burn_rate_gates: Immediate abort and rollback if burn_rate >= 4 for a 30-minute window (high severity)
Pause rollout at next increment if burn_rate between 1.5 and 4 sustained for 3 hours
Continue rollout if burn_rate < 1 for 24 hours
Predictive fast-fail: automated abort if a short-window (5m) modeled forecast predicts exceedance of error budget within next 2 hours
Tenant-sensitive gating: per-tenant burn_rate evaluation; global gate only if >50% of traffic cohorts show abnormal burn
graceful_degradation_playbook: Step 0 - Detect: Console alert triggers with P95 spike + model error-rate increase + KV cache miss surge
Step 1 - Non-disruptive mitigations: increase batching threshold, enable prefix cache for hot tenants, reduce concurrency on best-effort pool
Step 2 - Functional degradation (automated): route to quantized model variant with documented quality delta, limit max_tokens to configured band
Step 3 - Last-resort: route traffic to lower-tier fallback model or dedicated capacity with a customer-facing degraded mode banner
Step 4 - Rollback: if recovery not achieved in 2 hours post-degradation, perform automated rollback to previous model and halt rollout
acceptance_criteria: PRD and playbook approved by Eng, SRE, and Design
Console dashboards: per-tier SLO panels, per-tenant burn-rate trend, short-window predictive forecast visualization
Automated gating implementation (ENG) with a test harness that can simulate burn scenarios
Canary run: 10k synthetic requests across 3 regions demonstrating gate behaviors (no false-positive aborts in control runs)
Rollout policy config UI mock in Console reviewed by DX/Design
Runbook with PagerDuty escalation steps and customer communication templates completed
